evidence: M-O s.v. collection (marked as a modern sense)
terms.comment: Classically the act of gathering (Cic. Imp. Pomp. 22: membrōrum collēctiō), a summing-up in rhetoric and, in medicine, a swelling or abscess (Lewis & Short); the sense “things collected” is modern. A Roman named the things themselves, signa, tabulae, nummī, with colligere (see collect).

terms.gloss: a store, a treasure laid up
terms.comment: A hoard or store of valuable things; of a collection, a treasure of them.

terms.gloss: a collection of writings, a body of texts
evidence: Liv. 3.34.7: corpus omnis Rōmānī jūris (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The whole body of a set of writings or laws; first of all a body.

terms.gloss: a collection of rings and gems
terms.comment: A Greek word for a ring box (Mart. 11.59.4), which Pliny uses of a collection of gems.

phrases.latin: Gemmās plūrēs prīmus omnium Rōmae habuit — quod peregrīnō appellant nōmine dactyliothēcam — prīvignus Sullae Scaurus
phrases.english: The first man at Rome to own a collection of gems (they call it by a foreign name, a dactyliotheca) was Sulla’s stepson Scaurus

sources: Lewis & Short: collectio · Lewis & Short: thesaurus · Lewis & Short: corpus · Lewis & Short: dactyliotheca
